lines.trans: Listen up, right now we're shooting the scene where the main title appears.
You walk from over there toward here. The camera is behind you.
Once you walk up, stop right here. Stop and count three seconds.
After counting three seconds, turn back toward the camera. Got it?
She says she can't strip in a place like this, and asks where the subtlety is.
That's all about the contrast!
Hold on a second, calm down!
No fighting! Please stay quiet for a moment.
What happened?

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: いいか、今からタイトルが出るシーンを撮影する。
examples.trans: Listen up, right now we're shooting the scene where the main title appears.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: いいか、今からタイトルが出るシーンを撮影する。
examples.trans: Listen up, right now we're shooting the scene where the main title appears.

examples.text: いいか、このシーンは機密情報を奪う、この映画一番の見せ場だ！
examples.trans: Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!

examples.text: 前人未到のシーンをやるぞ！
examples.trans: We're pulling off a scene nobody has ever done before!

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Casual counterpart of こちら.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: 君たちは向こうからこっちに歩いてくる。カメラは背後だ。
examples.trans: You walk from over there toward here. The camera is behind you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 歩いてきたら、ここで立ち止まる。立ち止まって三秒数える。
examples.trans: Once you walk up, stop right here. Stop and count three seconds.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Derived from the verb 恥じる (to feel shy/ashamed).

examples.text: 彼女には恥じらいがある。
examples.trans: She has a sense of modesty.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Godan intransitive verb; 黙ってろ! is a rough 'Shut up!'.
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Interrogative prenoun adjectival; どのぐらい means 'about how much/many'.

examples.text: どのぐらいかかりますか。
examples.trans: About how long does it take?

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.
